name: OlmoBaseEval
intro: OlmoBaseEval 是 OLMo 3 为基础模型预训练与中训练决策设计的低噪声评测套件。论文 v2 从 70 个外部开放权重模型的约 2.3 万条分数出发，按模型排序相似性做 Ward 层次聚类，再以缩放信号和信噪比实验形成 Base Easy、六簇 Base Main 与四项发布前未使用的独立留出任务。
build_method: 候选任务池与 2.3 万分数汇集, Ward 排名相似性聚类与人工格式对齐, 缩放/信噪比筛选, Base Easy/Main 与独立留出集冻结
metric: 按任务使用 BPB、Accuracy、F1 或 pass@k；Base Main 汇总六个能力簇宏平均，留出任务单独报告
task_type: 基础模型综合评测, 问答, 数学, 代码
eval_feature: 预训练决策, 计算缩放, 能力簇聚合, 独立留出集
scale: 论文 v2：43 个具名评测项（Base Main 39 项 + 独立留出 4 项）；固定 OLMES 快照为 Base Main 38 项、含留出共 42 项；Base Easy 为复用标准续写的派生 BPB 代理
build_method_en: Candidate-task and 23K-score pool, Ward clustering by ranking similarity with manual format alignment, scaling/SNR selection, and frozen Base Easy/Main plus independent held-out tasks
eval_feature_en: Pretraining Decisions, Compute Scaling, Capability-cluster Aggregation, Independent Held-out Set
intro_en: OlmoBaseEval is OLMo 3's low-noise suite for base-model pretraining and midtraining decisions. Paper v2 starts from about 23K scores for 70 external open-weight models, clusters tasks with Ward linkage over model-ranking similarity, then uses scaling signal and signal-to-noise experiments to form Base Easy, six Base Main capability clusters, and four independent tasks never used before release.
scale_en: Paper v2 has 43 named entries: 39 Base Main plus 4 held-out; the fixed OLMES snapshot has 38 Base Main, 42 with held-out; Base Easy is a derived BPB proxy over reused gold continuations
metric_en: Task-specific BPB, accuracy, F1, or pass@k; six Base Main capability-cluster macro-averages, with held-out tasks reported separately

drawio_review_note:
reviewed_at=2026-07-18. Primary-paper boundary: Olmo 3, arXiv 2512.13961v2, fixed at https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.13961v2 and https://arxiv.org/pdf/2512.13961v2. The downloaded v2 PDF has SHA-256 f75208766c58a7eec434be61c93b5f7d904f2d2de31c02fca98dc9db0980fcae. The diagram follows section 3.3 and the task-configuration tables rather than inferring a generic dataset pipeline. OlmoBaseEval is an evaluation suite for compute-efficient pretraining and midtraining decisions, especially where small models, random-chance behavior, and noisy benchmarks can hide a useful development signal. Candidate coverage spans science, general knowledge, medical/laboratory knowledge, mathematics, code, and code fill-in-the-middle. The authors first assemble roughly 23K benchmark scores from 70 external open-weight models. Two tasks are treated as similar when they rank models similarly; Ward variance-minimizing hierarchical clustering merges them iteratively. The cut threshold is selected manually, same-format variants are moved together, and multiple-choice tasks are split into STEM and non-STEM, yielding six Base Main capability clusters: MC STEM, MC Non-STEM, GenQA, Math, Code, and Code FIM.

Scaling and selection boundary: paper experiments span about 10^18 through 10^25 training FLOPs, using 25 OLMo 2 scaling models in the low-compute range and the 70 open-weight models at higher compute. Base Easy is not another independent list of task rows: it derives negative log-likelihood per UTF-8 byte from gold or human continuations and is intended to produce signal below one billion parameters. Base Main preserves headroom for stronger models. Signal-to-noise is measured with the final 50 checkpoints of an OLMo 2 13B run and ten compute-matched external base models around 4×10^23 FLOPs, then checked again with intermediate checkpoints from five preliminary midtraining runs. Refinement expands selected 1K subsets to full datasets, removes BoolQ, leaves CruxEval outside the capability macro-average, and tunes pass@k for code. New components are BasicSkills with six tasks; Gen2MC over five QA sources, for which 200 validation samples per source were manually reviewed before full generation; multilingual MBPP across 17 programming languages; and masked perplexity over UltraChat and WildChat. MMLU Pro, DeepMind Math, LBPP, and BigBench Hard are reserved before release and are never used in development.

Count reconciliation is explicit and must remain visible: the paper enumerates 39 Base Main named task rows plus four held-out tasks, for 43 named entries; the pinned repository currently enumerates 38 Base Main rows and therefore 42 with held-out. Base Easy aliases reuse or derive continuations and do not add another independent paper count. In particular, MATH 500 is present in the paper tables but absent from the fixed suite code, while the repository uses mt_mbpp_v2fix. This is paper-code drift, not permission to rewrite the paper count. The pinned implementation is https://github.com/allenai/olmes/tree/5a51f502d463b8cdc4a2dcad7d7096c41ff1197e at commit 5a51f502d463b8cdc4a2dcad7d7096c41ff1197e. At that snapshot, oe_eval/configs/task_suites.py has SHA-256 b17d080412d7741dfe2be84742842265ecbe67f5f851cc3b476e25b9a676e92c and oe_eval/configs/tasks.py has SHA-256 a2e63e044af9b9fc47949647839852aeb435292319d6e0ebb14dddaf21edcfe7. README.md has SHA-256 62ef75fd8d50ac77cc62d076fb935b06702441cfa25a1726fef827eb3e0967df. LICENSE has SHA-256 62fb8a3a9621dc2388174caaabe9c2317b694bb9a1d46c98bcf5655b68f51be3 and identifies Apache-2.0; no release tag was used as the boundary.

Evaluation boundary: there is no single raw OlmoBaseEval dataset, single split, or universal prompt to claim. OLMES provides task-specific configurations, in-context-example counts, prompt formats, parsers, generation settings, and metrics. The paper tables use BPB for Base Easy and task-appropriate accuracy, F1, or pass@k for Base Main, then report six capability-cluster macro-averages and the held-out results separately. Mathematics and code generation use temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.6. The development experiments identify vLLM 0.9.0.1 and the final report identifies vLLM 0.11.0. The bilingual diagrams therefore separate the paper-v2 suite from the pinned OLMES implementation boundary and do not collapse version drift into a false single count. Formal publication evidence [site-a12a-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 3085×729 (English) and 3085×729 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 3083×728 and 3083×728. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
